subject.title: fix: external plugin tabs fail under gateway auth

question: Should authenticated Control UI read access mint route-scoped operator grants for external plugin iframes using this signed-cookie design?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent but intentionally introduces a new way for browser requests to exercise Gateway operator authority, so tests cannot substitute for maintainer ownership of the security model.

options.title: Approve after live proof
options.body: Accept the signed-cookie boundary after inspecting redacted browser diagnostics for matching, sibling, expired, and auth-rotation cases.

options.title: Choose a host-mediated proxy
options.body: Require the Control UI host to proxy authenticated plugin-tab traffic instead of issuing browser cookies, accepting the additional routing complexity.

options.title: Keep gateway-auth tabs unsupported
options.body: Retain the current 401 behavior and require external tabs to use plugin-managed or public routes rather than adding another credential surface.

recommendation.title: Approve after live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the signed-cookie boundary after inspecting redacted browser diagnostics for matching, sibling, expired, and auth-rotation cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to Gateway authentication, browser routing, plugin boundaries, and security policy.
